21960.etyen:
Alteration of hallo (“hello”) after hoi (“hey; ho”) and ohoi (“ahoy”).
The base hallo ultimately derives from German hallo (“hello; a call for attention”). Its further origin is uncertain; NAOB tentatively connects it with an older call associated with German holen (“to fetch”). The precise origin of hoi is likewise uncertain, while ohoi is from English ahoy.
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk halloi, Danish halløj and Swedish halloj (“hello, hi”).

1004744.etyen: From aust (“east, eastern”) + Gulen, literally “eastern Gulen”. The second element is of uncertain origin: Gulen has been derived either from Old Norse gul (“gust of wind”), or, more probably, from a Germanic root *geul reflected in Old Norse gjól (“cleft”). The surname is habitational, transferred from the place name.

1005000.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂m̥bʰi
Compound of vin (“wine”) + ambar (“wooden pail, wooden container”), literally “wine pail”. The first element vin (“wine”) is inherited from vín (“wine”), ultimately from vīnum (“wine”); the deeper origin of the Latin word is disputed. The second element ambar (“wooden pail, wooden container”) ultimately derives through Latin and Ancient Greek from a formation meaning “carried on both sides”; see ambar.
